summary: Iteration 2 focused on the INR migration, Sojaru logo, and 4 new homepage collection categories (New Arrivals, Featured, On Sale, Best Sellers). Backend: 25/25 pytest tests pass (added parametrized tests for the 4 category slugs/ids 29-32 with product presence, an explicit INR+₹ assertion on /api/store/config, and an INR price-range sanity check). Frontend: home renders header logo (/sojaru-logo.png, natural 659px), footer logo, prices in ₹ with Indian grouping (e.g. ₹1,499, ₹1,099, ₹2,999), NO $ anywhere, all four collection rows populated (32 product cards on home), 'New Arrivals' nav routes to /category/new-arrivals and shows products, PDP variation selection updates ₹ price, Add to Bag adds item, cart drawer shows ₹1,499 free-ship reference, /checkout country defaults to India, shipping = ₹99 (subtotal ₹999 < ₹1,499 threshold), order placed successfully with 'Complete Payment Securely' confirmation.

minor.issue: Fallback returns USD/$ if WooCommerce data/currencies/current is unreachable — could silently mask a store misconfig in prod.

ui_bugs.issue: Before size/color selection the price shows ₹0 (empty variation price). Consider showing the price range 'From ₹999' or the parent product price until a variation is picked.

integration_issues.issue: Checkout summary shows Subtotal ₹999 + Shipping ₹99 = Total ₹1,098, but the Woo-created order (and confirmation page 'Order total') is ₹999. The frontend does not send shipping_lines in the /api/orders payload, so WooCommerce records the order without the ₹99 shipping fee. User is charged the wrong amount if they trust the confirmation number.

action_items: Send shipping_lines (method_id='flat_rate' or 'free_shipping', total='99.00' or '0.00' based on threshold) in POST /api/orders so the WC order total matches what the customer saw at checkout. Otherwise the ₹99 shipping is silently dropped.
PDP: display 'From ₹<min>' or product base price instead of ₹0 before a variation is selected.
critical_code_review_comments: CheckoutPage.jsx computes shipping client-side (free>=1499 else 99) but the /api/orders body only carries line_items + billing + shipping address; no coupon_lines/shipping_lines. server.py forwards this to WC as-is, so Woo will re-compute totals (likely 0 shipping since no shipping method is passed) — leading to the ₹999 vs ₹1,098 mismatch observed on order confirmation.
server.py /api/store/config silently falls back to USD/$ on WC failure — with the app now hard-committed to INR this fallback is misleading. Prefer raising 502 or defaulting to INR/₹.
server.py still 456 lines and no retries on wc_request; noted in iteration 1, still true.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (25 tests, all passing). Category IDs are hard-coded (new-arrivals=29, featured-collection=30, on-sale=31, best-sellers=32) — update if the WC admin regenerates them. Known open bug from this iteration: /checkout shows total ₹1,098 (₹999 + ₹99 shipping) but the Woo order/confirmation shows ₹999 because /api/orders payload omits shipping_lines. To test after the fix: place an order with subtotal < ₹1,499 and confirm the confirmation-page 'Order total' equals checkout total; also test free-shipping path with subtotal >= ₹1,499 and confirm shipping = ₹0 both on checkout summary and Woo order.
rca of the issue: Root cause of the ₹99 shipping mismatch: /app/frontend/src/pages/CheckoutPage.jsx builds the /api/orders body from cart line items + billing/shipping addresses only. It never adds a shipping_lines entry. server.py::create_order() forwards this unchanged to POST /wp-json/wc/v3/orders. Because Woo receives no shipping method, it stores the order with 0 shipping — total = subtotal (₹999). The confirmation page reads the total back from the freshly-created Woo order, so the user sees ₹999 despite having reviewed ₹1,098 at checkout. Fix: in CheckoutPage before calling api.orders.create, compute shippingCents based on subtotal>=1499 and push shipping_lines: [{method_id: subtotal>=1499?'free_shipping':'flat_rate', method_title: subtotal>=1499?'Free shipping':'Flat rate', total: subtotal>=1499?'0.00':'99.00'}]. No backend change strictly required (OrderIn already tolerates extra keys via body.model_dump), but ideally add shipping_lines field to OrderIn for type-safety.
